title: XMSS Signatures
description: Signs with XMSS, the standardized stateful hash-based scheme built on Merkle trees of WOTS+ one-time keys. Security rests only on hash functions — no number theory for quantum computers to break. RFC 8391 and NIST SP 800-208 standardize it.
key_mechanisms: Sign with the next one-time key

demo.title: Demo — XMSS Signatures

title: LMS Signatures
description: Signs with LMS, the hash-based scheme using LM-OTS one-time keys in Merkle trees. Simpler than XMSS and standardized in RFC 8554; NSA recommends it for certain uses. It is the conservative post-quantum choice.

demo.title: Demo — LMS Signatures

title: Merkle Tree Construction
description: Builds the Merkle tree binding all one-time keys to one root public key. Leaves are one-time public keys; each parent hashes its children up to the root. The root is the long-term public key.

demo.title: Demo — Merkle Tree Construction

title: WOTS+ One-Time Signatures
description: Signs messages with Winternitz one-time signatures using hash chains. Each private-key element is hashed forward w times; the signature reveals intermediate values. One key signs exactly one message.

demo.title: Demo — WOTS+ One-Time Signatures

title: State Management Discipline
description: Manages the one-time-key index with crash-safe atomic updates. Reusing a one-time key breaks security catastrophically; the index must advance exactly once per signature, even across crashes. State handling is the whole ballgame.

demo.title: Demo — State Management Discipline

title: Multi-Tree XMSS^MT
description: Stacks XMSS trees in a hypertree so key generation stays fast for many signatures. Lower trees sign the roots of upper trees; total signatures multiply. It scales stateful signatures to millions of uses.

demo.title: Demo — Multi-Tree XMSS^MT

title: Key Generation Ceremonies
description: Generates hash-based keys in audited ceremonies with witnesses and recordings. The tree takes minutes to hours to build; the ceremony proves it was done honestly. Root keys are published widely.

demo.title: Demo — Key Generation Ceremonies

title: State Reservation
description: Reserves ranges of one-time keys for offline signers that cannot sync state. Each signer gets a disjoint range; exhaustion is tracked per range. It enables safe distributed signing.

demo.title: Demo — State Reservation

title: Backup and Restore
description: Backs up stateful keys without ever cloning the signing state. Restoring an old backup would reuse keys — catastrophic; backups store the key material plus the rule to never roll back. Cloning is forbidden.

demo.title: Demo — Backup and Restore

title: State Synchronization
description: Synchronizes signing state across redundant signers without reuse. A shared atomic counter or strict partitioning keeps signers disjoint. It is the hardest operational problem in stateful signatures.

demo.title: Demo — State Synchronization

title: Signature Verification
description: Verifies hash-based signatures statelessly with just the public key. Verification recomputes the Merkle path — no state needed on the verifier side. Anyone can verify with the standard algorithm.

demo.title: Demo — Signature Verification

title: NIST SP 800-208 Guidance
description: Follows NIST SP 800-208 for stateful hash-based signature use. The standard mandates state management practices and approved parameter sets. Compliance is required for federal use.

demo.title: Demo — NIST SP 800-208 Guidance

title: HSS Hierarchical Signatures
description: Uses HSS, the hierarchical LMS variant, for large signature counts. Levels of LMS trees sign the next level's roots; it mirrors XMSS^MT for LMS. RFC 8554 covers it.

demo.title: Demo — HSS Hierarchical Signatures

title: State Exhaustion Planning
description: Plans key rotation before the one-time key space runs out. Monitoring tracks consumption; new trees are generated and cross-signed well before exhaustion. Running out means no more signatures.

demo.title: Demo — State Exhaustion Planning

title: HSM Integration
description: Runs stateful signing inside HSMs with monotonic counters. The HSM enforces exactly-once state advancement in hardware; even a compromised host cannot reuse keys. It is the gold standard deployment.

demo.title: Demo — HSM Integration
